s: Who launched the Global Shield against Climate Risks at COP27?
x: The Global Shield was launched at COP27 by the G7 and V20 to give pre-arranged finance for climate disasters.

s: In which year was the New York Declaration on Forests first endorsed at the UN Climate Summit?
x: It was endorsed at the 2014 UN Climate Summit; it is voluntary and India was not an initial signatory.

s: Who launched the Global Methane Pledge at COP26?
o: the United States and the European Union
x: The US and EU launched the Pledge at COP26 to cut methane 30% from 2020 levels by 2030.

s: The International Drought Resilience Alliance was launched at which event and by which countries?
o: The Rio Earth Summit; India and Brazil
x: The International Drought Resilience Alliance was launched at COP27 by Spain and Senegal.

s: What is the goal of the New York Declaration on Forests?
o: To regulate persistent organic pollutants globally
To halt or reduce global forest loss
x: The New York Declaration on Forests aims to halt or reduce global forest loss.

s: By which year does the European Green Deal aim to make the EU net-zero in greenhouse gas emissions?
x: The European Green Deal targets net zero by 2050; Farm to Fork is one of its components.

s: By which year does the Early Warnings for All (EW4All) initiative aim to provide universal early-warning coverage?
x: EW4All aims to achieve universal early-warning coverage by 2027.

s: Which of the following is NOT a sector goal of the Glasgow Breakthroughs?
x: The Glasgow Breakthroughs cover power, road transport, steel, hydrogen and agriculture. Mercury management is associated with the Minamata Convention, not the Glasgow Breakthroughs.

s: What kind of body is The Climate Group, which runs RE100 and EV100?
o: Non-profit set up in London in 2003
x: The Climate Group is a London non-profit founded in 2003 that runs RE100 and EV100.

s: What does the Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC), founded in 2012 by UNEP and six countries, target?
x: CCAC (2012, UNEP plus six countries) works on short-lived climate pollutants.

s: By how much does the Global Methane Pledge seek to cut methane emissions by 2030, from 2020 levels?
x: The Global Methane Pledge targets a 30% cut from 2020 levels by 2030; India is not a member.

s: Which organisation is part of the coalition that runs the Climate Action Tracker, set up in 2009?
x: The Climate Action Tracker is an independent analysis run by research groups including Climate Analytics and NewClimate Institute.

s: Which voluntary initiative was launched by the UNFCCC Secretariat in 2015 to encourage climate neutrality?
x: Climate Neutral Now was launched by the UNFCCC Secretariat in 2015 and became a pillar of Momentum for Change.

s: Which organisation started Earth Hour?
x: Earth Hour was started by WWF in Sydney in 2007 and is held on the last Saturday of March.

s: Who founded 350.org, which organised the International Day of Climate Action on 24 October 2009?
x: 350.org was founded by Bill McKibben; it held the International Day of Climate Action on 24 October 2009.

s: The Clean Development Mechanism is provided under which Article of the Kyoto Protocol?
x: The CDM is Article 12 of the Kyoto Protocol; one CER equals one tonne of CO2-equivalent.

s: The Kyoto Protocol's first commitment period (2008-2012) required an average cut of about 5% below the levels of which year?
x: The first period set about a 5% (5.2%) cut below 1990; the Doha Amendment's 18% cut was also from 1990 levels.

s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the six gases originally covered by the Kyoto Protocol?
x: The original six gases were CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs and SF6. NF3 was added for the second commitment period.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Joint Implementation – Projects in developing countries
x: CDM yields CERs from projects in developing countries; Joint Implementation yields ERUs from projects in other Annex I countries.

s: Which country withdrew from the Kyoto Protocol in 2011?
x: Canada announced its withdrawal on 12 December 2011, effective 15 December 2012; it was the first country to leave Kyoto. The USA never ratified the Protocol.

s: Which instrument set the second commitment period of the Kyoto Protocol (2013-2020)?
x: The Doha Amendment (2012) set the second period with an 18% cut below 1990; it entered into force on 31 December 2020.

s: Under the Doha Amendment, what cut below 1990 levels did the second Kyoto commitment period require?
x: The second period (2013-2020) required an 18% cut below 1990; the first required about 5%.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Kyoto Protocol:
1. It set binding emission targets for Annex I countries only.
2. Canada was the first country to withdraw from it.
3. The USA ratified it in 2005.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Kyoto binds only Annex I countries and Canada was the first to leave (effective 2012); the USA never ratified it.

s: Which of the following countries never ratified the Kyoto Protocol?
x: The USA never ratified the Kyoto Protocol; Canada ratified it but later withdrew.

s: What are the credits issued under the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism established under Article 6.4 called?
x: Article 6.4 credits are called A6.4ERs. CERs are associated with the Kyoto Protocol’s Clean Development Mechanism.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Article 6.4 — UN-run Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism
Article 14 — Clean Development Mechanism under Kyoto
x: Article 6.4 establishes the UN-run Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism (PACM). Article 6.2 concerns bilateral cooperative approaches, while Article 14 concerns the Global Stocktake.

s: At which COP did Article 6 of the Paris Agreement become fully operational?
x: Article 6 was made fully operational at COP29; its 6.4 mechanism replaces the Kyoto CDM.

s: India signed the Joint Crediting Mechanism with Japan in August 2025 under which provision of the Paris Agreement?
x: The India-Japan Joint Crediting Mechanism, signed in August 2025, is a bilateral cooperative approach under Article 6.2. Its Rules of Implementation were adopted in January 2026. Article 6.4 is the UN-run PACM, Article 9.1 covers finance from developed countries and Article 14 is the Global Stocktake.

s: What is one carbon credit equal to?
x: One carbon credit equals one tonne of CO2 equivalent emitted, reduced or removed.

s: Which body issues Certified Emission Reductions (CERs)?
x: CERs are issued by the CDM Executive Board, not under the Nagoya Protocol.

s: In which country was the clean-cooking project that earned the first Article 6.4 credits?
x: The first Article 6.4 (PACM) credits went to a clean-cooking project in Myanmar, with South Korea.

s: What is the GHG Protocol?
o: An international accounting tool for governments and businesses to measure greenhouse gas emissions
An amendment to the Montreal Protocol to phase down HFCs
The UN-run carbon market under Article 6.4 of the Paris Agreement
A treaty to control mercury emissions
x: The GHG Protocol is an international accounting tool used by governments and businesses to measure greenhouse gases.

s: Under the Clean Development Mechanism, who runs emission-cutting projects and where?
o: developed countries in other developed countries
developing countries in other developing countries
x: Under Article 12 of Kyoto, developed countries run projects in developing countries and earn credits.

s: At which event did India launch the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI)?
o: The UN Climate Action Summit, 2019, New York
The UN Climate Action Summit, 2023, Dubai
x: India launched CDRI at the UN Climate Action Summit held in New York in 2019.

s: Which declaration was adopted at COP8, held in New Delhi in 2002?
o: Delhi Ministerial Declaration on Climate Change and Sustainable Development
BRICS Leaders' Framework Declaration on Climate Finance
x: COP8, held in New Delhi in 2002, adopted the Delhi Ministerial Declaration on Climate Change and Sustainable Development.

s:
Assertion (A): India's Panchamrit was associated with COP26.
Reason (R): COP26 included a reference to the phase-down of coal.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both are true of COP26 (Glasgow), but the coal phase-down language does not explain India's Panchamrit.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: COP29 — Baku — NCQG and finalisation of Article 6 rules
x: COP31 is scheduled for Antalya, Türkiye. Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, is associated with COP32, described as the Africa COP.

s: How was COP30, held at Belem in Brazil in 2025, described?
x: COP30 at Belem, Brazil, in 2025 was described as the “COP of Implementation”.

s: Which of the following correctly describes COP30?
o: It was held at Baku and finalised the Paris rulebook.
It was held at Belém, was the first COP in the Amazon and was called the COP of Truth.
It was held at Antalya and was designated the Africa COP.
It was held at Glasgow and adopted the Glasgow Climate Pact.
x: COP30 was held at Belém, Brazil, in 2025. It was the first COP in the Amazon and was called the COP of Truth.

s: Where was COP28 held in 2023?
x: COP28 (2023) was held at Dubai; Sharm el-Sheikh hosted COP27 and Baku the finance COP29.

s: Which one of the following was agreed at COP30?
o: To replace the Paris Agreement with the Belém Protocol
To work towards at least tripling adaptation finance
To make the Copenhagen Accord legally binding
To create the Loss and Damage Fund for the first time
x: COP30 agreed to work towards at least tripling adaptation finance. The Loss and Damage Fund had been created at COP27.

s: Where is COP31 in 2026 hosted?
x: COP31 (2026) is at Antalya, Türkiye; COP32 (2027) is at Addis Ababa.

s: Which of the following COP-host pairs is correctly matched?
x: COP24 was at Katowice; COP23 was at Bonn, COP25 at Madrid and COP16 at Cancun.

s: Which was the only COP hosted by India?
x: COP8 at New Delhi in 2002 is the only COP held in India; it adopted the Delhi Ministerial Declaration.

s: At which Conference of the Parties was the Kyoto Protocol adopted in 1997?
x: The Kyoto Protocol was adopted on 11 December 1997 at COP3 in Kyoto, Japan.

s:
Match the following COPs with their host cities:
List-I (COP)
A. COP20
B. COP22
C. COP23
D. COP29
List-II (Host city)
1. Bonn
2. Baku
3. Lima
4. Marrakech
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: COP20 was at Lima (2014), COP22 at Marrakech (2016), COP23 at Bonn under Fiji (2017) and COP29 at Baku (2024).

s: Which country held the presidency of COP25, which was held at Madrid in 2019?
x: COP25 was held in Madrid but under the presidency of Chile; COP23 at Bonn was under Fiji.

s: Which political, non-binding accord was the outcome of COP15 held in 2009?
x: COP15 at Copenhagen (2009) produced the Copenhagen Accord, a political, non-binding deal.

s: Which of the following energy pledges was associated with COP28?
o: Reducing renewable capacity to 4,000 GW and increasing efficiency gains to 11 per cent annually
Cutting methane by 30 per cent from 2020 levels and phasing out all coal by 2025
Providing 30 adaptation outcomes for four billion people by 2030
Tripling renewable capacity to 11,000 GW and doubling energy-efficiency gains to 4 per cent annually by 2030
x: COP28 included pledges to triple renewable capacity to 11,000 GW and double energy-efficiency gains to 4 per cent per year by 2030. The other options combine targets from different initiatives or alter the figures.

s: At which COP was the first Global Stocktake under Article 14 of the Paris Agreement concluded?
x: The first stocktake concluded at COP28 (Dubai, 2023), leading to the UAE Consensus; it is held every five years.

s: In connection with which event was Saraswathi of Malluvalasa in the news for sustainability work?
o: The Glasgow Leaders' Declaration on Forests and Land Use
The Global Renewables and Energy Efficiency Pledge
x: Saraswathi of Malluvalasa (Vizianagaram), known for natural farming and millet revival, was featured at Sustaina India 2025, a CEEW exhibition held in New Delhi in February 2025 (APPSC-GS 2024). She is not linked to a COP28 recognition.

s: Under the NCQG agreed at COP29, what is the legal nature of the call to reach US$1.3 trillion a year from all sources?
o: Binding only on Annex II countries
x: The US$1.3 trillion call is non-binding; the core goal is US$300 billion a year by 2035.

s: How many voluntary indicators under the Global Goal on Adaptation were adopted at COP30, Belém?
x: COP30 adopted 59 voluntary GGA indicators and an adaptation finance target of US$120 billion a year.

s: Which of the following was a historic outcome of COP27 held at Sharm el-Sheikh?
o: Adoption of the UAE Consensus calling for transition away from fossil fuels
Establishment of loss and damage funding arrangements, including a fund
Creation of the Joint Crediting Mechanism between India and Japan
Conclusion of the first Global Stocktake
x: COP27 produced a historic decision to establish loss and damage funding arrangements, including a fund. The UAE Consensus and the first Global Stocktake were outcomes of COP28.

s: Which was the first COP decision calling for transitioning away from fossil fuels in energy systems?
x: The UAE Consensus at COP28 was the first COP decision on transitioning away from fossil fuels in energy systems.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: AWARe — water initiative associated with COP27
MARS — global renewable-capacity pledge of COP28
Sharm el-Sheikh Adaptation Agenda — methane satellite alert system
Mitigation Work Programme — clean-cooking credit project in Myanmar
x: AWARe was a water initiative associated with COP27. MARS was UNEP’s methane satellite alert system, while the other pairings combine unrelated initiatives.

s: What was India's position on the NCQG core target of US$300 billion per year?
o: More than sufficient for developing countries
x: India criticised the US$300 billion annual NCQG target as inadequate.

s: At which COP was the Mitigation Work Programme, with at least two global dialogues a year to 2030, agreed?
x: COP27 at Sharm el-Sheikh set up the Mitigation Work Programme and reaffirmed the 1.5°C pursuit.

s: Under the New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) agreed at COP29, how much must developed countries provide or mobilise each year by 2035?
x: The NCQG core goal is at least US$300 billion a year by 2035 from developed countries; US$1.3 trillion is a broader non-binding call.

s: Which methane satellite alert system was launched by UNEP at COP27?
x: MARS (Methane Alert and Response System) is UNEP's satellite-based methane alert system launched at COP27; AWARe is the water initiative.

s: Which declaration made at COP28 in Dubai was not signed by India?
o: UAE Declaration on Climate and Health
Decision operationalising the Loss and Damage Fund
x: India did not sign the UAE Declaration on Climate and Health at COP28.

s: What does the 'Belém 4x pledge' made at COP30 aim to do?
x: The Belém 4x pledge at COP30 aims to quadruple sustainable fuels by 2035.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the UNFCCC?
o: It was adopted on 9 May 1992 at New York
It entered into force on 21 March 1994
Its Conference of the Parties is the supreme body and meets annually
Its secretariat is located at Geneva
x: The UNFCCC secretariat is at Bonn, Germany; Geneva hosts the IPCC secretariat.

s: Which are the two instruments adopted under the UNFCCC framework?
x: The Kyoto Protocol and the Paris Agreement are the two instruments associated with the UNFCCC; their governing meetings are referred to as CMP and CMA respectively.

s: When did the Kyoto Protocol enter into force?
x: Kyoto was adopted at COP3 on 11 December 1997 and entered into force on 16 February 2005.

s: When did the Paris Agreement enter into force?
x: The Paris Agreement entered into force on 4 November 2016. India ratified it on 2 October 2016.

s: To the development of which treaty did the first IPCC Assessment Report, published in 1990, contribute?
x: AR1 (1990) fed into the UNFCCC of 1992. The Convention was adopted on 9 May 1992 in New York and opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit in June 1992. Kyoto (1997), Paris (2015) and Montreal (1987) came later or deal with other issues.

s: Under the UNFCCC, which group is required to provide finance and technology to developing countries?
x: Annex II, the OECD members of Annex I, must provide finance and technology to developing countries.

s: On which idea does the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) rest?
o: Only developing countries must reduce emissions
All countries have identical historical responsibility and capabilities
Developed countries, having contributed most to historical emissions, should take the lead
Least developed countries must finance mitigation in OECD countries
x: CBDR-RC recognises differentiated historical responsibility and capabilities; developed countries that caused most historical emissions are expected to take the lead.

s: What is the primary aim of the UNFCCC?
o: Stabilise greenhouse gas concentrations at a level preventing dangerous anthropogenic interference with the climate system
Provide only financial assistance to small island developing States
Regulate international trade in endangered species
Eliminate all industrial production in developed countries
x: The objective of the UNFCCC is to stabilise greenhouse gas concentrations at a level that prevents dangerous anthropogenic interference with the climate system.

s: Where was the UNFCCC adopted on 9 May 1992?
x: The UNFCCC was adopted in New York and opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit in June 1992.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the CBDR-RC principle is correctly matched?
x: CBDR-RC appears in Rio Principle 7, UNFCCC Article 3.1 and Paris Agreement Article 2.2.

s: Where is the UNFCCC Secretariat located?
x: The UNFCCC Secretariat is at Bonn; the IPCC Secretariat is at Geneva.

s: On which date did India ratify the Paris Agreement?
x: India ratified the Paris Agreement on 2 October 2016; the Agreement entered into force on 4 November 2016.

s: What is the meeting of the Parties to the Paris Agreement called?
x: The Paris Agreement parties meet as the CMA; the Kyoto Protocol parties meet as the CMP.

s: At which event was the UNFCCC opened for signature in June 1992?
x: The UNFCCC was adopted in New York in May 1992 and opened for signing at the Rio Earth Summit in June 1992.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Convention on Biological Diversity – Biodiversity conservation
ITPGRFA – Plant genetic resources for food and agriculture
x: The Nagoya Protocol deals with Access and Benefit Sharing; biosafety and GMOs fall under the Cartagena Protocol.

s: Which convention is correctly matched with its year?
x: The CBD dates from 1992; Ramsar is 1971, the World Heritage Convention 1972 and the Cartagena Protocol 2000.

s: The Kigali Amendment (2016) is an amendment to which treaty, and what does it target?
o: Minamata Convention; mercury in dental amalgam
x: The Kigali Amendment (2016) to the Montreal Protocol phases down HFCs, which is why Montreal indirectly addresses GHGs. Kyoto has no Kigali amendment (CFCs are Montreal's), Basel deals with hazardous waste and Minamata with mercury.

s: Which one of the following treaties is NOT primarily concerned with reducing greenhouse-gas emissions?
x: The Basel Convention concerns the transboundary movement of hazardous waste, not greenhouse-gas reduction. The UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement address greenhouse-gas emissions and climate change.

s: What does the Montreal Protocol address?
x: The Montreal Protocol deals with ozone-depleting substances; hazardous waste is the Basel Convention's subject.

s: What does the Rotterdam Convention deal with?
o: Prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals and pesticides
x: Rotterdam covers prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals and pesticides; biosafety and GMOs come under the Cartagena Protocol.

s: Which treaty is correctly matched with its year?
x: Minamata dates from 2013; Montreal is 1987, Kyoto 1997 and Cartagena 2000.

s: In which year was CITES, known as the Washington Convention, signed?
x: CITES regulates international trade in endangered species and was signed in 1973.

s: Which of the following conventions directly addresses greenhouse gases?
x: The Kigali Amendment (2016) phases down HFCs, a greenhouse gas; Basel, Minamata and Rotterdam do not address GHGs.

s: What is the full form of INDC in climate negotiations?
x: INDC means Intended Nationally Determined Contributions under the Paris framework.

s: How often are Nationally Determined Contributions submitted under the Paris Agreement?
x: Each country sets its own NDC and submits it every five years; the targets themselves are not legally binding.

s: Under the Paris Agreement, what is the requirement that each new NDC show progression beyond the previous one called?
x: The ratchet mechanism requires each new NDC to progress beyond the last, informed by the Global Stocktake.

s: When did the United States leave the Paris Agreement for the second time?
x: The United States left the Paris Agreement for the second time in January 2026.

s: Which of the following is associated with Article 13 of the Paris Agreement?
o: The Enhanced Transparency Framework and Biennial Transparency Reports
The Global Stocktake every five years
The obligation to provide finance under Article 9.1
Withdrawal from the Agreement after notice
x: Article 13 establishes the Enhanced Transparency Framework, including common reporting through Biennial Transparency Reports. The first reports were due by the end of 2024.

s: Under Article 28 of the Paris Agreement, when may a party withdraw from the Agreement?
o: Three years after entry into force, with withdrawal taking effect one year after notice
Immediately after ratification, with effect on the same day
Only after unanimous consent of all other parties
Five years after entry into force, with effect after six months
x: A party may give notice of withdrawal three years after the Agreement entered into force for it, and the withdrawal takes effect one year after the notice. Unanimous consent is not required.

s: On which date did the United States re-enter the Paris Agreement?
x: The US withdrawal (announced 2017) took effect on 4 November 2020, and it rejoined on 19 February 2021.

s: Which one of the following is a stated feature of NDC 3.0?
o: It is economy-wide, covers all gases and is intended to align with 1.5°C.
It applies only to developed countries.
It is limited to carbon dioxide alone.
x: NDC 3.0 calls for economy-wide, all-gas pledges aligned with the 1.5°C objective and due for COP30.

s: Under Article 13 of the Paris Agreement, by the end of which year were the first Biennial Transparency Reports due?
x: Article 13 set up the Enhanced Transparency Framework; first Biennial Transparency Reports were due by end-2024.

s: How often does the Global Stocktake under Article 14 of the Paris Agreement take place?
x: The Global Stocktake is held every 5 years; the first concluded at COP28.

s: What is the emissions-intensity reduction target (from 2005 levels) by 2030 in India's updated NDC of 2022?
x: The 2022 update set 45% by 2030; the INDC had 33-35% and the 2031-35 NDC sets 47% by 2035.

s: What emissions-intensity reduction (from 2005) by 2030 did India's 2015 INDC target?
x: The 2015 target was 33–35%; it was raised to 45% in 2022, and the 2031–35 NDC targets 47% by 2035.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Paris Agreement:
1. It is a legally binding treaty.
2. The emission targets in each party's NDC are legally binding on that party.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Paris Agreement is a binding treaty, but only its procedures (prepare, communicate, report NDCs) bind; the NDC targets themselves do not.

s: Which part of the Paris Agreement is legally binding on its parties?
o: The duty to prepare, communicate and report NDCs
The emission-reduction target in each NDC
x: Only the procedural duties are binding; no party, whether the USA, China, India or the EU, is bound to its emission target.

s: What is the long-term temperature goal of the Paris Agreement?
o: Well below 2°C, pursuing 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels
x: The Paris Agreement aims to keep warming well below 2°C and to pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C.

s: On which date did the first withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement take effect?
x: The US announced withdrawal in 2017; it took effect on 4 November 2020, and the US rejoined on 19 February 2021.

s: When was the Loss and Damage Fund created and made operational?
o: created at COP27 and made operational at COP28
created at COP21 and made operational at COP22
created in 1991 and made operational in 2001
created under the Montreal Protocol and made operational at COP29
x: The Loss and Damage Fund was created at COP27 and became operational at COP28.

s: The Adaptation Fund is financed by what share of proceeds from CDM Certified Emission Reductions?
x: The Adaptation Fund gets a 2 per cent share of CDM CER proceeds.

s: Which losses does the Loss and Damage Fund cover?
o: Both economic and non-economic losses from sudden- and slow-onset events
x: The Fund covers economic and non-economic losses resulting from both sudden-onset and slow-onset events.

s: Where is the Green Climate Fund headquartered?
x: The GCF is headquartered at Songdo, Incheon (South Korea), not Washington, D.C.

s: Which institution serves as the interim host and trustee of the Loss and Damage Fund?
x: The World Bank is the interim host and trustee of the Fund for four years, until COP33 in 2028.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Global Environment Facility — established in 1991; headquarters at Washington, D.C.
Green Climate Fund — established in 1991; headquarters at Washington, D.C.
Adaptation Fund — established by the Montreal Protocol
Loss and Damage Fund — established under the Kyoto Protocol in 2001
x: The Global Environment Facility was established in 1991 and is headquartered in Washington, D.C.

s: The Board of the Loss and Damage Fund has how many members?
x: The Board has 26 members: 14 from developing and 12 from developed countries, deciding by consensus.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Global Environment Facility:
1. It was founded in 1991.
2. It is headquartered at Songdo, Incheon.
3. It finances the UNFCCC, CBD and Minamata Convention.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The GEF was founded in 1991, is headquartered at Washington DC and finances UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD, Stockholm and Minamata; Songdo is the GCF's HQ.

s: At which COP was the Green Climate Fund set up?
x: The GCF was set up in 2010 at COP16, Cancun, not Durban.

s: Which Indian institution is the National Implementing Entity of the Adaptation Fund?
x: NABARD is India's National Implementing Entity for the Adaptation Fund and Direct Access Entity for the GCF.

s: How many members does the Board of the Green Climate Fund have?
x: The Green Climate Fund has a 24-member Board; the Loss and Damage Fund Board has 26.

s: The Global Environment Facility finances which of the following groups of conventions and frameworks?
o: Only the CBD and Ramsar Convention
Only the UNFCCC and Paris Agreement
UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD, Stockholm Convention and Minamata Convention
Kyoto Protocol, CITES and Montreal Protocol exclusively
x: The GEF finances the UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD, Stockholm Convention and Minamata Convention, among others. It also houses the Global Biodiversity Framework Fund.

s: Where is the secretariat of the IPCC located?
x: The IPCC secretariat is located in Geneva.

s: Which bodies established the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) in 1988?
o: UNESCO and the International Union for Conservation of Nature
UNDP and the International Energy Agency
UNEP and the World Meteorological Organization
x: The IPCC was set up in 1988 by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).

s: Where is the headquarters of the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) located?
x: The WMO, a UN agency for weather and water, is headquartered in Geneva.

s: For a 50% chance of limiting warming to 1.5°C, what was the remaining carbon budget from 2020?
x: AR6 Working Group I placed the remaining carbon budget for a 50% chance of limiting warming to 1.5°C at about 500 GtCO2 from 2020.

s: When did the IPCC Seventh Assessment Report (AR7) cycle begin?
x: AR7 began in July 2023; Working Group reports are expected from about mid-2028.

s: Which one of the following is an India-relevant finding of the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (AR6)?
o: India's warming is confined to its coastal regions
India has experienced no significant change in heatwave intensity
India is warming more slowly than the global average
India is warming faster than the global average
x: The IPCC AR6 indicates that India is warming faster than the global average and is experiencing more frequent and intense heatwaves.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the IPCC?
o: It conducts original research independently of published literature
Its reports are policy-relevant but not policy-prescriptive
It shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore
x: The IPCC does not conduct original research; it assesses published literature.

s: Which document accompanies each IPCC assessment report to present its findings for policymakers?
x: The Summary for Policymakers accompanies each assessment report; it is not a legally binding instrument.

s: Which one of the following correctly matches an IPCC Working Group with its subject?
o: WG III — impacts, adaptation and vulnerability
x: WG I covers the physical science basis, WG II covers impacts, adaptation and vulnerability, and WG III covers mitigation.

s: The IPCC SR1.5 pathways require net CO2 emissions to fall about 45% by 2030 from the levels of which year?
x: The 45% cut by 2030 is measured from 2010 levels; SR1.5 was released in October 2018 and reaches net zero around 2050.

s: Which approach is inconsistent with the mitigation pathways described for limiting warming to 1.5°C?
x: The pathways require cuts that are deep, rapid and sustained; gradual or limited cuts are not sufficient.

s: Without immediate, deep emission cuts, when is the 1.5°C threshold likely to be crossed?
x: The AR6 assessment states that the 1.5°C threshold is likely to be crossed in the early 2030s without immediate, deep cuts.

s: In the AR6 mitigation pathway, renewables provide what share of global electricity by 2050?
x: The pathway needs emissions to peak before 2025, net zero by mid-century and 70–85% renewable electricity by 2050.

s: As cited in the IPCC AR6 India-relevant findings, by how much has the Gangotri Glacier retreated?
x: Gangotri has retreated about 1,700 m since 1935. 170 m since 1990, 17 km since 1850 and 700 m since 2000 misstate both the distance and the base year.

s: Shared Socioeconomic Pathways in AR6 replaced which set of scenarios used in AR5?
x: SSPs replaced the four Representative Concentration Pathways, or RCPs, used in AR5.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ocean and Cryosphere — oceans absorbed more than 90% of excess heat
Climate Change and Land — food security
Climate Change and Land — desertification and land degradation
Ocean and Cryosphere — reduction in the frequency of marine heatwaves
x: The Ocean and Cryosphere report highlighted that marine heatwaves became more frequent, along with coral bleaching and fisheries impacts. The other pairs are correctly matched.

s: How does black carbon deposited on snow mainly accelerate glacier melting?
o: preventing solar radiation from reaching the snow
x: Black carbon lowers the albedo of snow, causing it to absorb more solar energy and thereby accelerating melting.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: SSP3 represents Regional Rivalry. SSP1 represents Sustainability, SSP2 the Middle of the Road, SSP4 Inequality and SSP5 Fossil-fuelled Development.

s: With whom did the IPCC share the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize?
x: The IPCC shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore.

s: According to the IPCC SR1.5 (2018), between which years is warming likely to reach 1.5°C?
x: SR1.5 projected 1.5°C between 2030 and 2052, with net zero needed around 2050.

s: How much warming over 2011-2020 did the AR6 Synthesis Report record?
x: AR6 SYR (2023) assessed warming at 1.1°C over 2011-2020, with emissions at their highest ever.

s: Which of the following IPCC special reports is correctly matched with its subject?
o: SRCCL – Land use, desertification and food security
x: SRCCL (Aug 2019) covers land use, desertification, degradation and food security; SROCC covers oceans and the cryosphere.

s: On which subject is the Special Report of the IPCC AR7 cycle, planned for 2027?
x: AR7, begun in July 2023, includes a Special Report on Climate Change and Cities planned for 2027.

s: What does IPCC Working Group II deal with?
x: WG II covers impacts, adaptation and vulnerability; WG I is physical science and WG III mitigation.

s: What did the IPCC SROCC (2019) find about marine heatwaves?
x: SROCC found marine heatwaves more frequent and oceans holding over 90% of excess heat.

s: In which year was the IPCC's Fifth Assessment Report (AR5) released?
x: IPCC reports: AR1 1990, AR2 1995, AR3 2001, AR4 2007, AR5 2014; the AR6 Synthesis came in 2023.

s: From which body, set up in 1873, did the World Meteorological Organization originate?
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
x: The WMO grew out of the International Meteorological Organization (1873) and became a UN agency in 1951.

s: When was the Synthesis Report of the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report released?
x: The AR6 Synthesis Report came out on 20 March 2023, after the three Working Group reports of 2021-22.

s: According to the IPCC SR1.5 (2018), by about when must global net CO2 emissions reach net zero to limit warming to 1.5°C?
x: SR1.5 pathways cut net CO2 about 45% from 2010 by 2030 and reach net zero around 2050.

s: On what ground has India mainly criticised the EU CBAM?
o: eliminates all export costs for Indian producers
supports CBDR-RC and strengthens climate equity
violates CBDR-RC and represents green protectionism
applies only to domestic European production
x: India argues that CBAM violates the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) and amounts to green protectionism.

s: India sought dedicated agenda space at SB64 for discussion of which Paris Agreement provision?
o: Article 9.1 on finance by developed countries
Article 28 on withdrawal from the Agreement
x: India requested dedicated agenda space for Article 9.1, which obliges developed countries to provide climate finance to developing countries. Article 13 concerns transparency, while Article 28 concerns withdrawal.

s: At the Bonn SB64 session (June 2026), India aligned itself with which negotiating groups?
o: G77 and China, LMDC and BASIC
AOSIS, LMDC and the Umbrella Group
G77 and China, AOSIS and the EU
BASIC and the Environmental Integrity Group only
x: India aligned with G77+China (largest developing-country group), the LMDC (of which India is a member, hard-line on equity and CBDR) and BASIC. AOSIS is the small-island bloc pressing for 1.5°C, not India's group; the Umbrella Group and EU are developed-country groupings; 'BASIC only' leaves out G77 and LMDC.

s: Where was the Global Biofuels Alliance launched?
x: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched at the G20 New Delhi Summit (9-10 September 2023).

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: International Solar Alliance — COP21, 2015 — France and India
Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure — COP21, 2015 — France and India
Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure — COP26 — Gurugram
x: The International Solar Alliance was launched at COP21 (2015) by India and France and has its HQ at Gurugram. CDRI was launched by India at the UN Climate Action Summit in New York in 2019 and has its HQ in New Delhi.

s: Which one of the following is the largest negotiating group of developing countries in the UNFCCC process?
x: The G77 and China is the main and largest developing-country group. LMDC is a smaller hard-line group on equity and CBDR, BASIC has four members, and AOSIS is limited to small island states.

s: Which negotiating bloc in climate talks, made up of small island states, is known for pressing for the 1.5°C temperature goal?
x: AOSIS (Alliance of Small Island States) presses for the 1.5°C goal, as its members face existential threats from sea-level rise.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about climate equity?
o: India's per capita emissions are higher than those of industrialised nations
Developed countries emitted most of the historical stock of greenhouse gases
Developing countries argue that they need carbon space to grow
Climate justice recognises that those who emitted least may suffer the most
x: India's per capita emissions are much lower than those of industrialised nations.

s: Since when has India hosted the Voice of Global South Summits?
x: India has hosted the Voice of Global South Summits since January 2023 to press developing countries' needs for finance and technology; they are not a CBAM mechanism.

s: At COP26, India advocated which formulation regarding unabated coal power?
x: India advocated a phase-down, rather than a phase-out, of unabated coal power at COP26.

s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a mitigation constraint for India?
o: India's complete freedom from dependence on coal
Insufficient availability of appropriate alternative technologies
Need for growth and industrialisation for a large population in poverty
Inability to invest huge funds in research and development
x: India remains dependent on coal, so complete freedom from coal dependence is not a stated condition. Limited availability of alternatives, restricted R&D capacity and development needs are recognised constraints.

s: Which of the following is listed among India's coal-related mitigation measures?
x: India's coal measures include coal washing, ESPs, gasification, wet scrubbers, low-NOx burners and CCS/CCUS; ocean fertilisation is not among them.

s: Why is India's net-zero target of 2070 later than the 2050 target of most developed countries?
o: development needs and continuing dependence on coal
x: India links its later net-zero target to development priorities, a large population needing growth and industrialisation, and continuing coal dependence.

s: How did the 12th BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting held in New Delhi describe CBAM?
x: The 12th BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi, during India's chairmanship, called CBAM unilateral, punitive, discriminatory and protectionist.

s: What does Mission LiFE, associated with India's climate contribution, primarily seek to promote?
x: Mission LiFE is India's idea-level contribution centred on individual behaviour change.

s: India argues that developed countries should provide which of the following for its transition to cleaner development?
o: A waiver from all environmental obligations
Only military technology and concessional food aid
Clean and affordable technology and finance
x: India argues that developed countries should provide clean, affordable technology and finance to support the transition.

s: Where is the International Solar Alliance, the first intergovernmental body headquartered in India, located?
x: The ISA is headquartered at Gurugram.

s: Persons displaced by sea-level rise fall outside the scope of which of the following?
x: Climate refugees displaced by sea-level rise fall outside the legal scope of the 1951 Refugee Convention.

s: Apart from the Global Methane Pledge, which of the following did India not sign?
o: Glasgow Leaders' Declaration on Forests and Land Use
x: India stayed out of the Glasgow Leaders' Declaration on Forests and Land Use and the COP28 renewables pledge, and did not sign the Methane Pledge.

s: At which COP did India announce its bid to host COP33, later withdrawn in April 2026?
x: The PM announced the COP33 bid at COP28 on 1 December 2023; it was withdrawn in April 2026.

s: Which imports does the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) cover?
o: iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity
only crude oil and natural gas
x: CBAM covers imports of iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity.

s: India defends its net-zero target on the grounds of CBDR and development. What is the target year?
x: India's net-zero target is 2070, criticised as late but defended on CBDR and development grounds.

s: The BASIC group of countries in climate negotiations has how many members?
x: BASIC has four members; India attended its 19th meeting at Sun City.

s: In climate equity debates, what does the term 'carbon space' refer to?
o: Room for developing countries to grow
Forest area used as carbon sinks
Carbon budget left for developed countries
x: Carbon space means the room developing countries need to grow; historical responsibility points to developed countries' past emissions.

s: At which meeting was the Green Development Pact adopted?
x: The G20 New Delhi Summit (9-10 Sep 2023) adopted the Green Development Pact and launched the Global Biofuels Alliance.

s: India relies on domestic resources for about what share of its climate finance?
x: India relies mainly on domestic resources (about 83%); global climate finance was about USD 1.9 trillion in 2023.

s: What was India's rank in the Climate Change Performance Index 2019 (released December 2018)?
x: India was ranked 11th in CCPI 2019 (released at COP24, December 2018); 9th was its rank in CCPI 2020. ⚠ APPSC key said 9th.

s: LeadIT primarily works towards the low-carbon transition of which sectors?
x: LeadIT focuses particularly on low-carbon transitions in the steel and cement sectors and aligns heavy industry with the Paris goals.

s: The Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) is published by which group of organisations?
o: Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute and Climate Action Network International
x: The CCPI is published by Germanwatch, the NewClimate Institute and Climate Action Network (CAN) International.

s: Which coalition is correctly matched with its origin or launch?
o: International Big Cat Alliance – India and Sweden, 2019
Global Biofuels Alliance – India's G20 Presidency, 2023
x: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched during India's G20 Presidency in 2023; LeadIT was set up by India and Sweden (2019), Mission Innovation began at COP21 and the Big Cat Alliance was launched at Mysuru.

s: At which event was the Global Biofuels Alliance launched on 9 September 2023?
x: It came out of India's G20 Presidency, launched at the G20 New Delhi Summit.

s: Along with India and the USA, which country is a founding member of the Global Biofuels Alliance?
x: India, Brazil and the USA, together about 85% of world ethanol output, founded it.

s: Along with India, which country launched the Leadership Group for Industry Transition (LeadIT) in 2019?
x: LeadIT is an India-Sweden initiative of 2019; ISA is India-France.

s: Where was the International Big Cat Alliance launched in April 2023?
x: The International Big Cat Alliance was launched at Mysuru in April 2023.

s: Where did Mission Innovation, a clean-energy coalition, originate?
x: Mission Innovation began at COP21.

s: What was India's rank in the Climate Change Performance Index 2024?
x: India was 7th in CCPI 2024; 9th was 2020, 11th 2019 and 14th 2018.

s: In which edition of the Climate Change Performance Index was India ranked 9th?
x: 9th was India's CCPI 2020 rank; in CCPI 2019 India was 11th.

s: Where is the secretariat of the Global Biofuels Alliance located?
x: The Global Biofuels Alliance, launched at the G20 New Delhi Summit in 2023, has its secretariat in New Delhi.

s: The founding members of the Global Biofuels Alliance (India, Brazil and the USA) together produce about what share of the world's ethanol?
x: India, Brazil and the USA together account for about 85% of world ethanol output.

s: Where are the headquarters of the International Solar Alliance, the first international intergovernmental organisation headquartered in India?
x: The ISA Secretariat is at Gurugram, Haryana; New Delhi is linked with its founding conference.

s: Where was IRIS, the Infrastructure for Resilient Island States initiative, launched?
o: The UN Climate Action Summit in 2019
x: IRIS was launched at COP26 in 2021 and focuses on Small Island Developing States.

s: At which event was the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) launched in 2019?
x: CDRI was launched at the 2019 UN Climate Action Summit; its secretariat is in New Delhi and it is a partnership, not a treaty body.

s: The present membership principle of the International Solar Alliance is best represented by which one of the following?
o: Membership is restricted to countries between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn.
Membership is open to all United Nations member states.
Membership is restricted to countries that generate more than half of their electricity from solar power.
Membership is restricted to countries belonging to the European Union and SAARC.
x: Although the ISA initially began with the idea of bringing together sunshine countries between the tropics, its membership is now open to all UN member states.

s: Where and by whom was the International Solar Alliance launched on 30 November 2015?
o: at COP21, Paris, by India and France
at the UN Climate Action Summit, New York, by India alone
at COP26, Glasgow, by India and the UK
at New Delhi, as its Founding Conference
x: ISA was launched at COP21, Paris, on 30 Nov 2015 by India and France. The 2019 UN Climate Action Summit is where CDRI was launched; COP26 is linked to IRIS and Panchamrit; New Delhi hosted the Founding Conference on 11 March 2018, not the launch.

s: Where was the Founding Conference of the International Solar Alliance held?
x: ISA's Founding Conference was in New Delhi on 11 March 2018; it was launched at Paris in 2015.

s: Which of the following is an initiative of the International Solar Alliance?
o: One Sun One World One Grid
x: OSOWOG is an ISA initiative; IRIS belongs to CDRI.

s: Which of the following is NOT an initiative of the International Solar Alliance?
o: One Sun One World One Grid
x: IRIS (Infrastructure for Resilient Island States) is a CDRI initiative, not an ISA one.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The CDRI is a treaty-based intergovernmental organisation.
2. The CDRI is headquartered in New Delhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 2 is correct: CDRI is a partnership, not a treaty body; ISA is the treaty-based one.

s: As of March 2026, the International Solar Alliance has how many members?
x: ISA had 125 members by March 2026; Malta was the 119th, in February 2024.

s: Which is the apex decision-making body of the International Solar Alliance?
x: The ISA Assembly is the apex body.

s: As which member did Malta join the International Solar Alliance in February 2024?
x: Malta became the 119th member of the ISA in February 2024; membership reached 125 by March 2026.

s: Which country, which joined the International Solar Alliance in 2021, announced its exit in January 2026?
x: The USA joined the ISA in 2021 and announced its exit in January 2026.

s: In climate negotiations, India supports which principle?
o: Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities
Uniform emission-cut obligations for all countries
Equal net-zero year for developed and developing countries
x: India supports CBDR-RC and invokes equity and climate justice; it does not reject CBDR.

s: What is the target year of the Panchamrit commitment to meet 50 per cent of energy requirements from renewables?
x: The 50 per cent renewables target is for 2030; 2070 applies to the net-zero commitment.

s: Under net-zero emissions, what happens to residual greenhouse-gas emissions?
o: Required to fall to zero in gross terms
Balanced by removals such as forests and carbon capture
x: Net zero means residual emissions are balanced by removals such as forests and carbon capture, so gross emissions need not reach zero.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the quantitative memory sequence of the five Panchamrit commitments?
x: The Panchamrit sequence is 500 GW, 50 percent, 1 billion tonnes, 45 percent and net zero by 2070.

s: On what grounds does India mainly defend its comparatively later net-zero target?
o: Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and development needs
The absence of forest and tree cover
x: India invokes the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) and its development requirements to justify the 2070 target, later than the 2050 targets of most developed countries.

s: On which date did the Prime Minister announce the five commitments known as 'Panchamrit' at Glasgow?
x: The Panchamrit commitments were announced at Glasgow on 1 November 2021 during COP26.

s: India announced its target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070 at which international climate conference?
x: India announced its 2070 net-zero target at COP26 held in Glasgow in 2021.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Net Zero Portal (September 2026)?
o: It was launched with a NAPCC Dashboard tracking the national missions
Scope 1 and Scope 2 reporting is encouraged
It provides for mandatory disclosure of corporate net-zero targets
x: The portal is for voluntary, not mandatory, disclosure of corporate net-zero targets.

s: By which year is the Panchamrit pledge to cut projected emissions by one billion tonnes to be met?
x: The one-billion-tonne reduction is targeted for 2030, not 2050; 2070 is the net-zero year.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven transitions identified in India's LT-LEDS?
x: The seven transitions include low-carbon electricity systems, low-carbon transport, urban adaptation and efficient buildings, decoupling growth from industrial emissions, CO2 removal, forest and vegetation cover, and low-carbon finance. Expansion of fossil-fuel electricity systems is not one of them.

s: Under Panchamrit, what is India's non-fossil energy capacity target for 2030?
x: The first Panchamrit pledge is 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030 (hook 500-50-1-45-2070).

s: At which COP did India present its Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy (LT-LEDS)?
x: India presented its LT-LEDS at COP27 in November 2022.

s: When was the IEA's 'Net-Zero by 2050' roadmap released?
x: The IEA released its Net-Zero by 2050 roadmap in May 2021.

s: What was the base year adopted for India's Nationally Determined Contributions relating to the reduction of emissions intensity?
x: India's NDC commitments on emissions intensity use 2005 as the base year.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's 2015 INDC?
o: It targeted about 40% of installed electric capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030
It targeted 40% of total electricity generation from non-fossil sources by 2030
It proposed an additional carbon sink of 2.5–3 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent by 2030
It targeted a 33–35% emissions-intensity reduction by 2030
x: The 40% target concerned installed capacity, not actual electricity generation.

s: When did India communicate its updated NDC, which formalised the Panchamrit and added Mission LiFE?
x: The updated NDC was communicated in August 2022 with a 45% emissions-intensity target for 2030.

s: India's emissions intensity of GDP had fallen by what percentage below the 2005 level by 2020?
x: India achieved a 36% reduction in emissions intensity of GDP below the 2005 level by 2020.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
x: NDC 3.0 sets a 60% non-fossil installed-capacity share; 45% is the 2022 emissions-intensity target.

s: When did India submit its Intended Nationally Determined Contribution (INDC) to the UNFCCC?
x: India submitted its INDC to the UNFCCC in October 2015, before the Paris Climate Change Conference, COP21.

s: Who prepares India's NDCs and who gives their final approval?
o: NITI Aayog prepares them and Parliament approves them
The UNFCCC prepares them and MoEFCC approves them
MoEFCC prepares them and the Union Cabinet gives final approval
The Ministry of Power prepares them and the President approves them
x: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change prepares India's NDCs, while the Union Cabinet gives final approval.

s: When did the Union Cabinet approve NDC 3.0 for the period 2031–2035?
x: The Union Cabinet approved NDC 3.0 for 2031–2035 in March 2026.

s:
Assertion (A): India's updated NDC removed adaptation from its climate commitments.
Reason (R): Four of the eight missions under the NAPCC focus on adaptation.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Adaptation was not removed; it remains a key part of India's commitments, and four of the eight NAPCC missions focus on it.

s: Under its 2015 INDC, by how much did India pledge to cut the emissions intensity of its GDP by 2030?
x: The INDC target was 33-35% from the 2005 level; 45% is the 2022 update and 47% is NDC 3.0.

s: India's non-fossil target in its NDCs refers to the share of non-fossil sources in which measure of electricity?
x: The target is non-fossil installed capacity, not generation; generation is only about 25%.

s: What additional carbon sink did India's 2015 INDC target?
x: The INDC set a 2.5-3 bn t CO2e extra sink; 3.5-4 bn t is the NDC 3.0 target and 2.29 bn t is progress.

s: Under NDC 3.0, what is India's target for cutting the emissions intensity of GDP by 2035?
x: NDC 3.0 raises the intensity cut to 47% by 2035; 60% is its non-fossil capacity target.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's NDC 3.0:
1. It covers the period 2031-2035.
2. It targets a 60% non-fossil share of installed capacity.
3. It was approved by the Union Cabinet in March 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. NDC 3.0 was approved by the Cabinet in March 2026, not 2025.

s: By 31 December 2025, India and which other country were the only G20 members without a 2035 NDC?
x: India and Argentina were the only G20 members without a 2035 NDC by the end of 2025.

s: In which month and year did non-fossil sources cross 50% of India's installed electricity capacity?
x: India's non-fossil share of installed capacity crossed 50% in June 2025, ahead of the 2030 NDC target.

s: Under NDC 3.0 (2031-35), what additional carbon sink has India targeted?
x: NDC 3.0 raises India's extra carbon sink target to 3.5-4.0 billion tonnes CO2e, from 2.5-3 billion tonnes earlier.

s: About how much additional carbon sink had India created towards its NDC carbon sink target?
x: India had added about 2.29 billion tonnes CO2e of carbon sink against the 2.5-3 billion tonnes target.

s: Which two Panchamrit commitments entered India's August 2022 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC)?
o: 500 GW non-fossil capacity and net zero by 2070
45 percent emissions-intensity reduction and 50 percent renewable-energy commitment
One billion tonnes reduction and 500 GW capacity
Net zero by 2070 and one billion tonnes reduction
x: The August 2022 NDC took in two Panchamrit pledges: a 45% cut in emissions intensity of GDP (from 2005) and the 50% target, written as a 50% non-fossil share of installed capacity, both by 2030.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's non-fossil electricity position?
o: More than 50% of installed capacity was non-fossil by 2025
The non-fossil generation share necessarily equals its installed-capacity share
Limited storage keeps the non-fossil generation share low
About 25% of electricity generated was non-fossil
x: Installed capacity and actual generation are different measures, so their shares need not be equal.

s: The National Green Hydrogen Mission is associated with which outlay and production target?
o: ₹1.97 lakh crore; 5 MMT a year by 2070
x: The mission has an outlay of ₹19,744 crore and targets 5 MMT/year capacity by 2030, supporting energy independence by 2047 and net zero by 2070. The other options either change the target (50 or 10 MMT) or the outlay, or confuse the 2047/2070 goals with the target year.

s: Forest and tree cover constituted approximately what proportion of India’s geographical area in 2021?
x: Forest and tree cover accounted for approximately 24.6 percent of India’s geographical area in 2021.

s: The Nuclear Energy Mission aims to establish how many indigenous small modular reactors by 2033?
x: The mission targets five indigenous small modular reactors by 2033.

s: Which statement on India's pumped storage capacity is correct?
o: 25.8 GW identified; 17 GW operational; 7 GW more planned by 2030
258 GW identified; 7 GW operational; over 17 GW more planned by 2030
7 GW identified; 258 GW to be commissioned by 2030
258 GW operational; no addition planned by 2030
x: India's identified pumped storage potential is 258 GW, with 7 GW operational and more than 17 GW additional capacity planned by 2030.

s: Which one of the following is identified as a key programme for achieving the carbon-sink target in India's LT-LEDS?
x: The Green India Mission is identified as a key programme for the carbon-sink target in the LT-LEDS.

s: In which state is the Pinnapuram integrated renewable energy and pumped storage project located?
x: Pinnapuram, a 1,680 MW integrated RE plus pumped storage project, is in Andhra Pradesh.

s: What is the capacity of the Pinnapuram integrated renewable energy and pumped storage project?
x: Pinnapuram in AP is a 1,680 MW project; 180 MW is Gujarat's first standalone BESS.

s: In which state is India's first standalone battery energy storage system, of 180 MW?
x: India's first standalone BESS (180 MW) is in Gujarat.

s: What is the carbon-sink area target under the Green India Mission?
o: 5 Mha new plus 5 Mha improved forest
2.5 Mha new plus 2.5 Mha improved forest
x: The Green India Mission aims at 5 million hectares of new and 5 million hectares of improved forest/tree cover.

s: MISHTI, a carbon-sink programme, targets about 540 sq km of which ecosystem?
x: MISHTI targets about 540 sq km of mangroves.

s: What is India's position on the Global Methane Pledge?
x: India has not signed the Global Methane Pledge.

s: As per IRENA 2026, what is India's rank in renewable energy capacity?
o: Third, after China and the USA
Fourth, after China, USA and Brazil
x: India is 3rd in RE capacity, after China and the USA.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Mission LiFE?
o: LiFE stands for Lifestyle for Environment
LiFE is written into India's NDC 3.0
It shifts the focus from individual behaviour to state action
x: Mission LiFE shifts the focus the other way: from state action to individual behaviour and mindful consumption.

s: Where was Mission LiFE launched in October 2022?
x: Mission LiFE was launched at Kevadia with the UN Secretary-General; the idea was introduced at COP26, Glasgow (2021).

s: Mission LiFE lists 75 LiFE actions under how many themes?
x: Mission LiFE has 75 actions under 7 themes, such as save energy and save water.

s: With which areas are UJALA and PAT respectively associated?
o: Single-use plastic bans and e-waste recycling
Water conservation and sustainable food systems
x: UJALA is associated with LED bulbs, while PAT is an industrial-efficiency initiative aligned with LiFE.

s: What does 'P3' stand for in Mission LiFE?
x: LiFE's P3 approach means Pro-Planet People.

s: At which COP did India first put forward the idea of LiFE?
x: The LiFE idea came at COP26 in 2021, not COP25; the Mission was launched in October 2022.

s: On which date was the LiFE Global Movement launched?
x: The LiFE Global Movement began on 5 June 2022; the Mission itself was launched in October 2022 at Kevadia.

s: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme was designed to contribute to which intensity-reduction target?
x: The scheme was designed to meet the 45 percent intensity target.

s: Which body administers India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS)?
o: Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
x: The CCTS is run by the BEE under the Ministry of Power; ICFRE administers the Green Credit Programme.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Green Credit Programme (GCP)?
o: It is administered by ICFRE, Dehradun
It was launched under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001
It rests on the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
x: The GCP rests on the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986; the Energy Conservation Act (Section 14AA) is the basis of the CCTS.

s: For what kind of actions is the Green Credit Programme a market-based incentive mechanism?
x: The programme rewards voluntary environmental actions; its afforestation credits can be exchanged for compensatory-afforestation obligations.

s: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme of India combines which of the following mechanisms?
o: A compliance mechanism and an offset mechanism
A voluntary mechanism and an import mechanism
A taxation mechanism and a subsidy mechanism
A conservation mechanism and a litigation mechanism
x: The Indian Carbon Market combines a compliance mechanism for energy-intensive sectors with an offset mechanism for voluntary projects in ten sectors.

s: Under the compliance mechanism of the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, what happens to an obligated entity that performs better than its notified GHG Emission Intensity target?
o: Must purchase additional Carbon Credit Certificates
Receives a Carbon Credit Certificate that can be traded
Receives a direct compensation from the Union Budget
Is exempted from all environmental regulations
x: Entities that beat their notified GHG Emission Intensity targets earn tradeable Carbon Credit Certificates. Entities that miss their targets must buy certificates.

s: What does the United Kingdom's recognition of India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) mean?
o: CCTS counts as a qualifying carbon price under the UK CBAM from 1 January 2027, avoiding double charging of Indian exports
Indian exporters are fully exempt from all UK import duties from 2026
CCTS credits can be used to meet EU CBAM obligations
The UK will administer the CCTS jointly with the Bureau of Energy Efficiency
x: CCTS is a qualifying carbon price under the UK CBAM (from 1 Jan 2027), so Indian exports are not charged twice. It does not remove all import duties, concerns the UK (not EU) CBAM, and CCTS remains administered by BEE alone.

s: Why is the Khasi Hills Community REDD+ project in Meghalaya significant?
o: Compensatory-afforestation project under the Green Credit Programme
x: The Khasi Hills Community REDD+ project is India’s first Plan Vivo-certified REDD+ project.

s: What kind of carbon market is India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme?
o: Exclusively a voluntary market for households
x: CCTS sets emission-intensity targets, not an absolute cap on emissions.

s: By reducing which emissions did the Surat Emissions Trading Scheme show the effectiveness of market-based regulation?
x: The Surat Emissions Trading Scheme reduced particulate-matter emissions by 20–30 percent.

s: From which law does the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme derive its legal basis?
o: Section 14AA of the Energy Conservation Act, 2001
The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
x: CCTS rests on Section 14AA of the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 (amended 2022); the GCP rests on the EPA 1986.

s: How many obligated entities were notified under the CCTS by October 2025?
x: 282 entities in sectors such as aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali and pulp and paper were notified.

s: Against what can afforestation under the Green Credit Programme be exchanged?
x: GCP afforestation credits are exchangeable for compensatory afforestation.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Green Credit Programme – run by BEE
Green Credit Programme – Energy Conservation Act, 2001
x: CCTS was notified in June 2023 and is run by BEE; the GCP is run by ICFRE under the EPA 1986.

s: From which date does the UK CBAM recognise India's CCTS?
x: The UK CBAM recognises CCTS from 1 January 2027.

s: Which of the following is India's first mandatory compliance carbon market?
x: The CCTS (notified June 2023, run by BEE) is India's first mandatory compliance market; the Green Credit Programme rewards voluntary actions.

s: How have the State Action Plans on Climate Change evolved?
o: From district-specific adaptation plans to broad mitigation plans
From broad mitigation plans during 2010–15 to district-specific, risk-based adaptation plans from 2020 onwards
From national mitigation plans to plans unrelated to local institutions
From risk-based plans during 2010–15 to purely sector-neutral plans after 2020
x: States have moved from broad mitigation-centric plans in 2010–15 towards district-specific, risk-based adaptation plans from 2020 onwards, linked with social schemes and local institutions.

s: How many State Action Plans on Climate Change are approved and operational?
x: 34 SAPCCs (28 States + 6 UTs) are approved and operational.

s: What fix has been proposed for the financing weakness of SAPCCs?
o: Climate budgeting through State Finance Departments
Funding only through the coal cess
x: Finance is the SAPCCs' weakness; climate budgeting via State Finance Departments is the proposed fix.

s: Who heads Tamil Nadu's Governing Council on Climate Change?
x: Tamil Nadu has a Governing Council on Climate Change headed by the CM, plus the TN Green Climate Company.

s: Under which mission are the State Climate Change Centres that support SAPCCs set up?
o: National Mission for Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem
National Mission on Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change
x: State Climate Change Centres come under NMSKCC.

s: In which year did Fridays For Future Andhra Pradesh take part in its first global climate strike?
x: FFF-AP joined its first global climate strike in 2019.

s: Under which Department does the Andhra Pradesh State Climate Change Cell function?
x: AP's exclusive Climate Change Cell (November 2022) works under the Department of Environment, Forests and Science & Technology.

s: Which period does the revised Andhra Pradesh State Action Plan on Climate Change cover?
x: The revised AP SAPCC covers 2025–30 and includes eight energy-sector adaptation measures.

s: Which one of the following correctly represents the green-cover targets of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Andhra Pradesh has set an interim green-cover target of 37% by 2030 and a target of 50% by 2047.

s: In August 2026, the AP State Climate Change Cell prescribed how many energy-sector adaptation measures?
x: APSCCC prescribed eight energy-sector adaptation measures for AP-Genco, NREDCAP and AP Green Energy Corporation.

s: In which year did the AP National Green Corps programme begin?
x: AP National Green Corps began in 2002-03; the national NGC began in 2001-02.

s: What did the Andhra Pradesh Government create in November 2022 to deal exclusively with climate change?
x: AP created an exclusive Climate Change Cell in November 2022; it is now the AP State Climate Change Cell (APSCCC).

s:
Consider the following sectors:
1. Water
2. Agriculture
3. Health
Which of the above are identified as vulnerable to climate hazards in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Heatwaves, droughts, floods and cyclones put water, agriculture, food security and health at risk in Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)?
o: It is a framework concerned exclusively with greenhouse-gas mitigation.
It deals only with air-pollution control in urban areas.
It is limited to biodiversity conservation and wildlife protection.
It is an overarching domestic framework addressing both mitigation and adaptation.
x: The NAPCC is India’s overarching domestic climate framework and covers both mitigation and adaptation. It is not confined exclusively to greenhouse gases, biodiversity or air pollution.

s: In which year was the Prime Minister's Council on Climate Change, under which the NAPCC was prepared, constituted?
x: The Council was constituted in 2007; the NAPCC was released on 30 June 2008 by PM Dr Manmohan Singh.

s: Through which of the following are India's NDCs delivered domestically?
o: The National Adaptation Plan, national missions and SAPCCs
SAPCCs that replace the national missions
x: NDC implementation is pursued through the National Adaptation Plan, the national missions and State Action Plans on Climate Change.

s: The National Action Plan on Climate Change serves as India’s domestic vehicle for which international climate commitment?
x: The NAPCC is the domestic vehicle for implementing India’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).

s: How did India's adaptation spending change as a share of GDP between FY16 and FY22?
x: Adaptation spending rose from 3.7% of GDP (FY16) to 5.6% (FY22). The reversed option swaps the years, the 0.37/0.56 option misplaces the decimal, and 1.2/2.5 is incorrect.

s: Which Prime Minister released the National Action Plan on Climate Change on 30 June 2008?
x: Dr Manmohan Singh released the NAPCC on 30 June 2008.

s: How many of the eight core NAPCC missions focus on adaptation?
x: Four of the eight missions focus on adaptation.

s: Where was CoP30, at which India delivered its National Statement on 17 November 2025, held?
x: CoP30 was held at Belem in Brazil; India gave its National Statement there on 17 November 2025.

s: By which year does India aim to achieve net zero emissions?
x: India's Nuclear and Green Hydrogen missions advance its goal of net zero by 2070.

s: Which one of the following is one of the original eight National Missions under the NAPCC?
o: National Mission for Sustaining the Coastal and Marine Ecosystem
x: The National Water Mission is one of the eight; Clean Air, wind and coastal missions are not NAPCC missions.

s: The National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency includes which of the following schemes?
x: The Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme is included in the National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency and is associated with the Ministry of Power and BEE.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the two DST missions under the NAPCC?
o: NMSHE assesses Himalayan vulnerability across 12 thematic areas
NMSKCC supports Centres of Excellence and State Climate Change Centres
Both missions have the Ministry of Jal Shakti as their nodal ministry
x: Both missions are under the Department of Science and Technology, not the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

s: The National Solar Mission was launched on 11 January 2010 with an objective of achieving what capacity by 2022?
x: The National Solar Mission was launched on 11 January 2010 and targeted 100 GW of solar capacity by 2022.

s: Which NAPCC mission is correctly matched with its nodal ministry?
o: National Mission on Sustainable Habitat – Ministry of Jal Shakti
National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture – Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare
National Water Mission – Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
National Mission for a Green India – Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
x: NMSA is under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare; NMSH is under MoHUA, the Green India Mission under MoEFCC and the National Water Mission under Jal Shakti.

s: In which year was the National Solar Mission launched?
x: The Solar Mission was launched on 11 January 2010, not 2008 when the NAPCC was released.

s: The National Mission for Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem covers how many thematic areas?
x: NMSHE covers 12 thematic areas; NMSKCC covers 4.

s: Which is the nodal ministry for the National Mission on Sustainable Habitat?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
x: MoHUA is the nodal ministry for the National Mission on Sustainable Habitat.

s: When did the CCEA approve the Green India Mission?
x: The CCEA approved the Green India Mission on 20 February 2014.

s: Which is the nodal ministry for the National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency?
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
x: NMEEE is under the Ministry of Power and is run through the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE).

s: Which is the nodal ministry for the National Solar Mission under the NAPCC?
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: The National Solar Mission (JNNSM), launched on 11 January 2010, is run by the MNRE.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a sub-mission of the Green India Mission?
o: Expansion of forest and tree cover and ecosystem restoration
Improvement of incomes of forest-dependent people
x: The three sub-missions concern forest quality, forest and tree cover with ecosystem restoration, and incomes of forest-dependent people. Thermal power generation is not a GIM sub-mission.

s: How does the Green India Mission respond to climate change?
x: By expanding and restoring forest cover, the Green India Mission tackles both adaptation and mitigation.

s: Besides a public water database, on which areas does the National Water Mission focus?
x: NWM goals include a public water database and a focus on over-exploited areas, with a 20% gain in water-use efficiency.

s: Under the Perform, Achieve and Trade mechanism, what do energy-intensive units that exceed their energy-saving targets receive?
o: Energy Saving Certificates that can be traded
Carbon tax rebates issued by State governments
x: PAT rewards industries that beat their energy-saving targets with tradable Energy Saving Certificates.

s: Under the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture, Soil Health Cards are issued free every:
x: Soil Health Cards are issued free every two years; micro-irrigation gets up to 55% subsidy.

s: What gain in water-use efficiency does the National Water Mission aim at?
x: The NWM seeks a 20% gain in water-use efficiency.

s: Up to what share is the micro-irrigation subsidy under the NMSA?
x: NMSA offers up to 55% micro-irrigation subsidy.

s: Through which scheme has the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture been implemented since 2022-23?
x: NMSA moved from Green Revolution-Krishonnati (2018-19) to PM-RKVY from 2022-23.

s: What shortfall did the CAG audit of August 2026 find in the Green India Mission's cover-increase component?
x: Cover increase fell short by 97.57%; 91.87% was the shortfall in quality improvement.

s: What is the full form of PAT, the market mechanism under the National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency?
x: PAT stands for Perform, Achieve and Trade; units that beat their targets earn tradable Energy Saving Certificates.

s: What additional carbon sink by 2030 is targeted under the Green India Mission?
x: The Green India Mission targets an additional sink of 2.5-3.0 bn t CO2e by 2030; 50-60 Mt is its extra annual sequestration target for 2020.

s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture?
x: NMSA components are Rainfed Area Development, On-Farm Water Management, Soil Health Management and the Sub-Mission on Agroforestry; PAT belongs to NMEEE.

s: Which institution launched the India Climate Change Knowledge Portal in 2020 as a supporting tool for tracking climate-related actions?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: The India Climate Change Knowledge Portal was launched in 2020 and tracks ministry-wise climate actions; it is associated with the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

s: The NAPCC Dashboard, launched in September 2026, is intended primarily to perform which function?
o: Replace the State Action Plans on Climate Change
x: The NAPCC Dashboard was launched in September 2026 to track the progress of the national climate missions.

s: Which is the nodal unit for UNFCCC negotiations and NAPCC coordination?
x: The MoEFCC Climate Change Division is the nodal unit; the PM's Council sets policy and the Executive Committee coordinates.

s: Under whom does the Executive Committee on Climate Change, the NAPCC coordination body, function?
x: The Executive Committee coordinates under the Principal Secretary to the PM; the PM's Council handles policy.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Executive Committee on Climate Change – UNFCCC negotiations
PM's Council on Climate Change – Policy
India Climate Change Knowledge Portal – September 2026
x: The PM's Council sets policy; the Climate Change Division handles negotiations, the Net Zero Portal takes disclosures and the Knowledge Portal dates from November 2020.

s: Which is the National Implementing Entity for the National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change?
x: NABARD is the NIE for NAFCC; CCAP (2014) is an MoEFCC capacity-building scheme.

s: In which year was the National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (NAFCC) set up?
x: NAFCC was set up in 2015 as a central sector scheme; 2017 is when the coal cess went into the GST compensation cess.

s: In 2017, into which cess was the clean energy cess that funded the National Clean Energy Fund folded?
x: The cess, levied on coal since 2010-11, was folded into the GST compensation cess in 2017.

s: Which body runs the Climate Change Action Programme (CCAP), a capacity-building scheme launched in 2014?
x: CCAP is a MoEFCC scheme of 2014 that supports SAPCCs; NABARD implements NAFCC.

s: On which of the following was the clean energy cess that financed the National Clean Energy Fund levied?
x: NCEF (2010-11) came from a clean energy cess on coal, merged into the GST compensation cess in 2017.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. NAFCC is a central sector scheme for adaptation projects of States/UTs.
2. NABARD is the implementing agency of the Climate Change Action Programme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 1 is correct: NABARD is NAFCC's National Implementing Entity; CCAP is run by MoEFCC.

s: What is the full form of NAFCC?
o: National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change
National Action Fund for Clean Climate
National Agency for Forest and Climate Change
National Adaptation Framework for Coastal Communities
x: NAFCC is the National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (2015); NABARD is its National Implementing Entity.

s: The Economic Survey 2025–26 describes the NAPCC as having nine missions. To what does the additional mission relate?
x: The extra mission is on climate change and human health; the core-mission count remains eight.

s: Which set lists the missions proposed for the NAPCC around 2015?
o: Wind Energy, Health, Coastal Areas, Waste-to-Energy
Wind Energy, Clean Air, Nuclear, Green Hydrogen
Coastal Areas, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Health
x: Wind Energy, Health, Coastal Areas and Waste-to-Energy were proposed; only Health has reached the list.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the NAPCC's missions?
o: Health is the mission added in the Economic Survey count
The Economic Survey 2025-26 counts ten missions
A Coastal Areas mission was proposed around 2015
