x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 counts nine missions, not ten; the core missions remain eight.

s: On which of the following does the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute mainly focus?
x: NEERI (Nagpur, CSIR) works on environmental science and engineering. Clearances, tribunals and forest diversion belong to other bodies.

s: Where is the Zoological Survey of India headquartered?
x: ZSI, like the Botanical Survey of India, is in Kolkata; Dehradun hosts the Wildlife Institute of India.

s: The Central Pollution Control Board was established in 1974 under which legislation and was renamed in 1988?
o: Environment Protection Act; renamed as the National Green Tribunal
Water Act; renamed as the Central Pollution Control Board
Air Act; renamed as the National Pollution Board
Wildlife Protection Act; renamed as the Wildlife Board
x: The CPCB was established in 1974 under the Water Act and was renamed in 1988. Its headquarters are in New Delhi.

s: Where is the Central Arid Zone Research Institute (CAZRI) located?
x: CAZRI is at Jodhpur; ICFRE is in Dehradun, IIFM in Bhopal and BNHS in Mumbai.

s: Which body is associated with delivering environmental justice?
x: The NGT delivers environmental justice; CPCB controls pollution, NBA implements the BD Act and NTCA handles tigers.

s: Where is INCOIS located?
x: INCOIS is in Hyderabad; NBA is in Chennai, WII in Dehradun and BNHS in Mumbai.

s: Which of the following is the apex body in the national forestry research system?
o: Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE)
x: ICFRE (Dehradun) is the apex body of India's forestry research system. FRI, IIFM and CAZRI are institutes under it or elsewhere.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Biodiversity Authority implements the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.
2. The Centre for Biodiversity Policy and Law, within the NBA at Chennai, is an India–Norway collaboration.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Both are true: the NBA (Chennai) implements the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, and its Centre for Biodiversity Policy and Law is an India–Norway project.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The National Environmental Engineering Research Institute is located in Nagpur.
It was earlier known as CPHERI.
It functions under the National Green Tribunal.
x: Option C is incorrect: NEERI in Nagpur, earlier CPHERI and set up in 1958, is a CSIR laboratory, not part of the NGT.

s: Where is the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI) located?
x: NEERI, a CSIR lab, is at Nagpur.

s: Where is the Centre for Science and Environment (CSE), an environment NGO, based?
x: CSE is in New Delhi; BNHS is in Mumbai.

s: The roots of the Forest Research Institute (FRI) can be traced to which institution and year?
o: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services, 1999
x: FRI Dehradun grew from the Imperial Forest Research Institute of 1906. BNHS dates from 1883 and INCOIS from 1999.

s: Where is the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) located?
x: WII, the wildlife research and training body, is at Dehradun, like FRI and ICFRE.

s: In which year was the Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS) founded?
x: BNHS, based in Mumbai, was founded in 1883; 1906 is FRI, 1958 is NEERI and 1982 is IIFM.

s: In which year was the Survey of India, the national mapping agency, set up?
x: The Survey of India, under the DST, was set up in 1767; it is a mapping agency, not an environment body.

s: The Bhopal gas tragedy took place during which period and involved the leakage of which substance?
x: The Bhopal gas tragedy occurred on 2–3 December 1984 when methyl isocyanate leaked from Union Carbide’s pesticide unit. More than 2,500 deaths were reported in the cited assessment.

s: What mostly causes industrial disasters such as Bhopal (MIC) and LG Polymers (styrene)?
x: Industrial disasters are mostly caused by toxic gas leaks; radioactive leaks such as Chernobyl are a separate category.

s: The Los Angeles smog episode of 1943 was primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Photochemical smog formed by sunlight acting on nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons from vehicle exhaust
Methyl mercury released into an industrial water body
Radioactive pollution caused by a reactor leak
Classical smog caused by sulphur dioxide and water vapour at low temperature
x: The Los Angeles smog was photochemical smog, produced when sunlight acted on nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons from vehicle exhaust, particularly at about 24–32°C.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Chernobyl — Radioactive leak from a reactor
LG Polymers, Visakhapatnam — Styrene vapour leak
x: Fukushima involved a hydrogen explosion and radioactive leak after an earthquake-tsunami. The styrene vapour leak occurred at LG Polymers in Visakhapatnam in 2020.

s: Which substance leaked at LG Polymers, Visakhapatnam on 7 May 2020?
x: LG Polymers leaked styrene vapour; Bhopal was methyl isocyanate.

s: In which country was Chernobyl at the time of the 1986 disaster?
x: Chernobyl was in the USSR in 1986; it is now in Ukraine, not Russia.

s: Which of the following was the London smog of December 1952 an example of?
x: London 1952 was classical smog (water vapour plus SO2/H2S at low temperature); Los Angeles 1943 was photochemical.

s: From whose wastewater did the methyl mercury that caused Minamata disease come?
x: Chisso Corporation's wastewater released methyl mercury at Minamata.

s: In which city of Andhra Pradesh did the LG Polymers styrene gas leak of 7 May 2020 occur?
x: The leak occurred at R.R. Venkatapuram in Visakhapatnam.

s: In which year did the styrene vapour leak at LG Polymers, R.R. Venkatapuram, Visakhapatnam take place?
x: The LG Polymers styrene leak took place on 7 May 2020, the most recent major industrial disaster in AP.

s: Which disaster of 2011 involved a hydrogen explosion and radioactive leak after an earthquake and tsunami?
x: Fukushima (Japan, 2011) had a hydrogen explosion and radioactive leak after the earthquake-tsunami.

s: Chemical fertilisers and pesticides are a major primary source of which type of pollution?
x: Fertilisers and pesticides mainly cause soil pollution; sewage discharge is the main source of water pollution.

s: Eutrophication and fish kills are impacts of which type of pollution?
x: Water pollution from sewage and effluents causes water-borne diseases, eutrophication and fish kills.

s: What is the main cause of water pollution?
o: Industrial emissions of SO2 and NOx
x: Sewage is the main source of water pollution (APPSC 2025); fertilisers and pesticides are the main source of soil pollution.

s: According to the WHO, air pollution causes about how many deaths a year?
x: WHO puts air pollution deaths at about 7 million a year; 3.8 million is household air pollution.

s: Which of the following represents a secondary pollutant?
x: Secondary pollutants are formed by reactions in the environment. Ozone and peroxyacyl nitrate are examples, whereas plastics are listed as primary pollutants in the classification table.

s: Insecticides and herbicides are examples of which type of pollutants?
x: Insecticides and herbicides are qualitative pollutants; CO2 is a quantitative pollutant.

s: A thermal plant chimney, vehicles along a highway, a mining area and farm runoff are respectively examples of which types of pollution source?
x: By source geometry: a chimney is a point source, a highway with vehicles is a line source, a mining area is an area source and farm runoff is a diffuse (non-point) source. Option A alone gives this order; B swaps chimney and highway and also mining and runoff, C swaps highway and mining, D swaps chimney and mining.

s: What are xenobiotics?
o: Only radioactive elements released by reactors
Synthetic chemicals foreign to living systems that resist degradation
Naturally occurring nutrients essential to all organisms
x: Xenobiotics are synthetic chemicals foreign to living systems, such as pesticides, PCBs and plastics, and they generally resist degradation.

s: Plastics and DDT are examples of which type of pollutants?
x: Plastics and DDT resist natural disposal; sewage and heat are biodegradable.

s: Which of the following is a secondary pollutant?
x: PAN, like ozone, forms by reactions in the air, so it is a secondary pollutant.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: SO₂ is associated with acid rain and air pollution.
CFCs or Freon are associated with ozone depletion.
x: Option B is incorrect: DDT is non-biodegradable and persists, building up in food chains. SO₂, N₂O and CFCs are correctly linked to their effects.

s: Up to what level has MoEF&CC capped lead in household and decorative paints?
x: The cap is 90 ppm, not 900 ppm; lead from vehicles and smelters can cause brain damage.

s: Burning tyres, plastics, flex and e-waste in open fires can release which combination of pollutants?
o: Ozone and peroxyacyl nitrate without other pollutants
Dioxins, furans, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and toxic metals
x: Such burning can release dioxins, furans, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, lead, cadmium and mercury.

s: In the NCR, where do about 77-80% of ammonia emissions come from?
x: Fertilisers and livestock account for 77-80% of ammonia in the NCR.

s: From which source are brominated flame retardants, which are persistent and endocrine-disrupting, mainly released?
x: Brominated flame retardants in electronics, plastics, foam and textiles are released from e-waste.

s: What does lead from motor vehicles and smelters mainly cause?
x: Lead damages the brain; MoEF&CC caps lead in paints at 90 ppm.

s: Which heavy metals are found in coal ash, whose disposal pollutes soil?
o: Arsenic, mercury, lead, cadmium and chromium
x: Coal ash carries toxic heavy metals such as arsenic, mercury, lead, cadmium and chromium into the soil.

s: Which of the following is a source of mercury pollution?
x: Mercury is released by coal combustion, smelters and chemical effluents.

s: Against the open burning of tyres, plastics and e-waste during which festival did the APPCB issue an advisory in January 2026?
x: APPCB's 11 January 2026 advisory warned that Bhogi bonfires release dioxins, furans and toxic metals.

s: Synthetic paints used on idols are a source of which heavy metals?
x: Mercury, cadmium and lead are released from synthetic idol paints.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Marble cancer — acid rain caused by sulphur dioxide
x: Marble cancer is associated with acid rain, particularly sulphur dioxide. Biomagnification is associated with DDT, the greenhouse effect with carbon dioxide, and lung cancer with asbestos or particulates.

s: With which component of the Taj Mahal's marble does acid rain react to damage it?
x: Sulphuric and nitric acids in acid rain react with the calcium carbonate of marble.

s: Sulphur hexafluoride (SF6) is an extremely potent greenhouse gas because it:
o: Is used as an electrical insulator
Absorbs infrared and lasts thousands of years
x: SF6's potency comes from absorbing infrared and persisting for thousands of years; its insulator use is unrelated.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Biomagnification is linked to DDT; CFCs cause ozone depletion.

s: What is the rise in the concentration of a persistent pollutant at each higher trophic level called?
x: Biomagnification is the rise at each trophic level; bioaccumulation is build-up within one organism.

s: What is the build-up of a persistent pollutant inside a single organism over time called?
x: Bioaccumulation happens within one organism; biomagnification across trophic levels.

s: In a food chain, where is the highest load of a biomagnified pollutant such as DDT found?
o: Top consumers such as fish-eating birds
x: Concentration rises at each trophic level, so top consumers carry the highest load.

s:
Consider the following statements about biomagnification:
1. DDT and mercury are typical biomagnifying pollutants.
2. In Minamata, methyl mercury was biomagnified in fish.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: DDT and mercury biomagnify, and methyl mercury in fish caused Minamata disease.

s: At which conference was the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) created?
x: The 1972 Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment created UNEP.

s: At which conference was Agenda 21 adopted?
x: Agenda 21 came out of the 1992 Rio Earth Summit; Rio+20 reaffirmed it.

s: 'The Future We Want' is the outcome document of which conference?
x: Rio+20 (2012) produced the non-binding document 'The Future We Want'.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The UN Conference on the Human Environment was held in Stockholm in June 1972.
2. Agenda 21 is a legally binding treaty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 1 is correct: Agenda 21 is a non-binding action plan for the 21st century.

s: With which institution did the CPCB develop the Comprehensive Environmental Pollution Index (CEPI) in 2009?
x: CEPI was developed with IIT Delhi and scores clusters 0-100 for air, water and land.

s: Which one of the following CEPI classifications is correctly matched?
x: A CEPI score of 70 or above indicates a critically polluted cluster. Scores from 60 to below 70 indicate severe pollution.

s: In which State is Patancheru-Bollaram, classified as critically polluted under CEPI, now located?
x: Patancheru-Bollaram was then in AP and is now in Telangana; Visakhapatnam was another AP cluster assessed.

s: What are the three factors used in the Comprehensive Environmental Pollution Index?
x: CEPI scores clusters on pollutant, pathway and receptor (exposed people).

s: In the 2009 CEPI assessment, how many of the 88 clusters were critically polluted?
x: 43 of 88 clusters were critically polluted (score 70 or above) in 2009.

s: CPCB's 2016 colour categorisation of industries is based on a Pollution Index of which factors?
o: Water pollution, air pollution and hazardous waste
x: The Pollution Index is a function of water and air pollution and hazardous waste generation.

s: What is the Pollution Index of a Red category industry under CPCB's 2016 scheme?
x: Red is 60 and above; Orange 41-59, Green 21-40, White 20 and below.

s: The 2025 revision of CPCB's industry categories added which colour category?
x: The 2025 revision added a Blue category.

s: Which city of Andhra Pradesh was assessed under the Comprehensive Environmental Pollution Index (CEPI)?
x: Visakhapatnam is the AP industrial cluster assessed under CEPI.

s: Which category of industries is treated as practically non-polluting under CPCB's 2016 colour scheme?
x: White category industries have a Pollution Index of 20 and below and are practically non-polluting.

s: Which of the following developments is correctly matched with its environmental governance significance?
o: Environment Audit Rules 2025 — introduction of third-party auditors
PARIVESH 3.0 — abolition of all environmental clearances
PARIVESH 3.0 — separate portals for every environmental approval
Environment (Protection) Fund Rules — 25% retained by State governments
x: The Environment Audit Rules 2025 introduced third-party auditors. PARIVESH 3.0 is a single-window system, while 25% of the Environment (Protection) Fund is kept by the Centre.

s: What is PARIVESH 3.0?
x: PARIVESH 3.0 is the single-window clearance system; third-party auditors come under the Environment Audit Rules 2025.

s: What share does the Centre keep under the Environment (Protection) Fund Rules?
x: The Centre keeps 25% under the Environment (Protection) Fund Rules.
